content: Polyethylene glycol 3350 is a medication prescribed to treat occasional constipation. It belongs to a class of drugs known as osmotic laxatives. This medication works by retaining water in the stool, which increases the frequency of bowel movements and softens the stool, making it easier to pass. Polyethylene glycol 3350 is available as a powder that must be mixed with a liquid and taken orally. It is typically taken once daily as needed for up to two weeks. You should carefully follow the instructions on your prescription label and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take this medication exactly as directed. It is important to note that polyethylene glycol 3350 can be habit-forming. Do not take larger doses, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer duration than prescribed by your doctor. It may take 2 to 4 days for this medication to produce a bowel movement. To use the powder form of polyethylene glycol 3350, follow these steps: If using the medication from a bottle, measure a single dose (approximately one heaping tablespoon) using the measuring line on the bottle cap. If using packets, each packet contains a single dose. Pour the powder into a cup containing 8 ounces of water, juice, soda, coffee, or tea. Stir the mixture until the powder dissolves completely. Drink the solution immediately. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before taking polyethylene glycol 3350, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to polyethylene glycol or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had a bowel obstruction (a blockage in the intestine) or if you experience symptoms of bowel obstruction, such as an upset stomach, vomiting, stomach pain, or bloating. Additionally, inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. To support the effectiveness of this medication, maintain a well-balanced diet that includes fiber-rich foods such as unprocessed bran, whole-grain bread, and fresh fruits and vegetables. Drink plenty of fluids and engage in regular physical activity. If you forget to take a dose, this medication is typically taken as needed, so you can take it when required. Polyethylene glycol 3350 may cause side effects. Mild side effects include upset stomach, bloating, cramping, and gas. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, though uncommon, may include diarrhea or hives. If you experience these symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. If you notice any unusual problems while taking this medication, consult your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Symptoms of overdose may include diarrhea, thirst, confusion, or seizures. Keep all appointments with your doctor while using this medication. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
